A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SKEWD research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are readable and support matching retained content despite substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B report original causal-discovery experiments on synthetic and established bivariate benchmarks, including an ECM ablation.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B retain those experiments and add original multivariate graph-recovery results, CAREFL evaluations, and marginal-density ablations.

M1.justification: v2 extends the bivariate method to SKEWD-MV: multivariate additive spline models with covariate-specific penalties, PC-based estimation of a Markov equivalence class, and likelihood-based selection among its DAGs. It also introduces evaluated variants using KDE instead of Gaussian marginal densities.

E1.justification: v2 adds multivariate causal-graph recovery on synthetic six- and ten-node LSNMs, substantially extending v1's bivariate direction-identification task. The original 13 established benchmarks and six grouped skew-noise benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: The new graph experiments compare SKEWD-MV against HOST, GraN-DAG++, and CAM. Section 6.1 also newly reports CAREFL evaluations on skewed LSNMs, Tübingen, and SIM benchmarks, although CAREFL is omitted from the main comparison tables. The original bivariate comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces 100 generated datasets per graph size, each with 1,000 observations, and evaluates SHD, SID, precision, recall, and F1 with estimated versus oracle equivalence classes. It specifies exclusions for five failed GraN-DAG++ runs and zero-precision/recall cases in baseline F1 averages. The reported ECM convergence window also changes from one to 25 iterations; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B.6 adds extensive Gaussian-versus-KDE marginal ablations across bivariate and multivariate experiments. The oracle-equivalence-class comparison additionally probes the contribution of graph-estimation errors. The existing ECM ablation and residual-independence case study are retained.

E5.justification: The original across-benchmark standard-deviation summaries remain unchanged. v2 adds no seed-based repetitions, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests for comparative performance. Its additional graph tables report means without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in v1 Tables 1-8 match v2 Tables 1 and 3-9. Substantial new results cover CAREFL, graph recovery, and KDE variants. For example, v2 Table 2 reports SKEWD-MV mean SHD of 2.27 and 4.72 for six and ten nodes; Table 13 reports SIM accuracy of 76% with KDE versus 54% with Gaussian marginals. These are additional comparisons, not improvements to unchanged-version scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition 5.1 and its proof establishing equivalence of partial and full likelihood maximization within a Markov equivalence class. It formalizes multivariate LSNMs and additive-model penalties and adds the restricted-HNM conditions underlying prior multivariate identifiability results. The original marginal-likelihood proof and bivariate identifiability theorem remain.

C1.justification: v1 presents bivariate causal discovery and lists multivariate inference as future work. v2's abstract, contribution list, and conclusion explicitly extend the contribution to likelihood-based causal-graph discovery, while retaining the original skewness-robustness claims.

C2.justification: New discussions explain noise-family selection, robustness beyond the skew-normal tail range, and when KDE helps or harms causal scoring. Sections 5.3-5.4 add substantive scalability and misspecification limitations. Future-work boundaries now include interaction effects and multivariate independence-based inference rather than multivariate discovery generally.

D1.justification: v2 adds multivariate spline sizes, five-fold cross-validation, a 3,000-iteration ECM limit, PC's kernel independence test, implementation caching/parallelization notes, and KDE bandwidth selection. However, it omits v1's 40 initial and 20 additional Bayesian-optimization candidates, log-search range, and acquisition-function specification. Hardware and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds discussion of differentiable DAG learning and score matching, including Zheng et al., Lachapelle et al., and Rolland et al., alongside references supporting PC, additive models, and graph metrics. Several background references are removed, but the central positioning against symmetric-noise LSNM methods remains.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and introduction, converts the contributions to a list, moves Related Work before the method, and relocates Bayesian-optimization exposition to Appendix B. It substantially reorganizes the modeling, inference, experiments, and appendices into numbered subsections.

P2.justification: v2 adds graph-comparison and marginal-ablation displays in Tables 2 and 10-16, plus Algorithm 2. It adopts an ICML proceedings layout with running headers, revised typography, caption placement, and plot sizing. The original nine figures and eight result tables remain, with the tables partly renumbered.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves multivariate discovery and non-Gaussian marginals as future work. v2 supplies a graph algorithm with a supporting scoring proof and comparative experiments, while controlled KDE ablations replace speculation about marginal assumptions with evidence of both benefits and failures. This substantially strengthens applicability and understanding of limitations while preserving the original results. Validation remains confined to small synthetic graphs, and some optimization details disappear, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the gains.
